reviewer: Codex (automated evidence review; human approval via pull request)

facts: Chrome 153 documents user-activated camera and microphone controls with browser-owned permission UI.
XPlayer is a playback component; its inspected code contains no capture API.
xtendHypotheses: A capture component needs separate permission and media-track ownership.
records.decisionRationale: No capture requirement or cross-engine evidence authorizes a new production component.

facts: WebKit TP 252 fixes delayed streaming Fetch response-body delivery; stable Safari availability is not established.
iterateResponseBody reads incrementally; the HTTP AppService transport parses bounded NDJSON frames.
xtendHypotheses: A delayed-two-frame browser fixture can distinguish browser buffering from XTend handling.
records.decisionRationale: Retain the accepted response-streaming path. Preview evidence does not justify a timeout or transport change.

facts: Firefox 155 documents WebTransport send groups, priority controls and graceful session draining.
XScaler owns stream sessions and cleanup; RMT has backpressure metadata. The inspected paths contain no WebTransport integration.
xtendHypotheses: Mapping Fabric lanes to network priority requires explicit fairness, delivery and cancellation decisions.
records.decisionRationale: Require a separate transport ADR and fallback evidence before product adoption.

facts: Firefox 155 documents retryable network and MIME module-load failures at the same specifier.
tryLoad marks tags loaded after success; XScaler cleans up failed or aborted module scripts and enforces SRI.
xtendHypotheses: A bounded same-URL recovery lab should separate network/MIME errors from evaluation and security failures.
records.decisionRationale: Retain cache-busting, SRI and abort protections; one engine does not authorize automatic retry policy.

facts: Chrome 154 Beta documents WritableStream HTML insertion methods, including safe and unsafe variants.
RMT commits DOM descriptors and owns trusted-HTML and no-manual-HTML boundaries. Its renderer has no streamAppendHTML sink.
xtendHypotheses: Native parser streaming may alter ownership, Custom Element upgrade order and hydration identity; writer backpressure does not prove Fabric compatibility.
records.decisionRationale: Architecture review required: determine whether a safe sink can remain behind trusted descriptor ownership. Require an isolated lab; no unsafe/script-enabled production paths.

facts: Safari Technology Preview 251 added backpressure when uploading a stream request body with fetch(), but Technology Preview evidence is not stable Safari shipping.
Chromium has shipped request streaming since 105 with duplex: half plus redirect, CORS and HTTP/2-or-newer restrictions.
Firefox request streaming remains an in-development engine issue rather than a shipping feature.
XTend Maraca still sends buffered JSON request envelopes and only streams NDJSON responses; NFM-BPR-019 therefore keeps fetch-request-streaming at reject-for-now.
xtendHypotheses: A request-side streaming contract may later extend the host-injected Maraca HTTP transport, but the current Search Worker is not the relevant network boundary.
records.decisionRationale: No new raw evidence authorizes additional product adoption. Preserve September ADRs and accepted members; this intake disposition does not reverse them.

facts: Chrome 141 shipped Navigation API precommit handlers in its stable channel.
Safari Technology Preview 251 added precommitHandler and NavigationTransition.to, which is preview evidence rather than stable Safari shipping.
A rejected precommit handler cancels the navigation before URL commit and the hook is available only for cancelable navigation events.
XTend x-router still owns guards, cancellation, DOM commit, focus and announcements; no Navigation API adapter exists in the reviewed tree.
The new preview evidence does not satisfy the target-engine and router-parity requirements behind NFM-BPR-015, so navigation-api remains reject-for-now.
xtendHypotheses: A lab-only host adapter could compare precommit guards and post-commit focus behavior with the existing x-router lifecycle without changing router ownership.
records.decisionRationale: No new raw evidence authorizes additional product adoption. Preserve September ADRs and accepted members; this intake disposition does not reverse them.

facts: Chrome 152 shipped declarative shadowrootreferencetarget and imperative ShadowRoot.referenceTarget in its stable channel.
Mozilla records a positive standards position, while its implementation tracker remains open and does not establish Firefox shipping.
The WebKit standards-position request remains open without stable Safari evidence.
XTend has Shadow DOM and hydration accessibility contracts but no referenceTarget path in the reviewed tree.
The terminal 24-parent Radar has no atomic member for this capability; a raw AI verdict cannot add one automatically.
xtendHypotheses: A test-only fixture could compare host-name fallback with reference-target naming before hydration, after activation and after reconnect.
records.decisionRationale: No new raw evidence authorizes additional product adoption. Preserve September ADRs and accepted members; this intake disposition does not reverse them.

facts: Chrome 152 shipped Connection Allowlists in its stable channel.
The response header constrains outgoing connections for a document or worker before connection establishment and provides a report-only variant.
Mozilla records a positive standards position, but neither that position nor the open WebKit request establishes non-Chromium shipping.
XTend already owns application-level remote-origin checks and a connect-src CSP, but has no Connection-Allowlist header synthesis.
The capability is single-engine and absent from the terminal Radar taxonomy, so the report's prototype_now verdict remains non-binding.
xtendHypotheses: A report-only server fixture could compare manifest-derived endpoints with the existing remote-surface and Maraca policies without changing runtime defaults.
records.decisionRationale: No new raw evidence authorizes additional product adoption. Preserve September ADRs and accepted members; this intake disposition does not reverse them.

facts: Chrome 153 lists JavaScript Self-Profiling Markers as a new origin trial rather than stable browser shipping.
The marker proposal adds an optional sample category for script, gc, style, layout, paint or other browser work.
Marker access is restricted to cross-origin-isolated contexts, and the base profiler checks the js-profiling-mode or js-profiling Document Policy.
XTend already records stream-pressure samples and exposes performance telemetry snapshots, but it has no JavaScript Self-Profiling or marker ingestion path.
xtendHypotheses: A future opt-in test-only adapter could correlate aggregated marker categories with existing Fabric lane and backpressure telemetry without exposing trace format or sampling data as a stable runtime contract.
records.decisionRationale: No new raw evidence authorizes additional product adoption. Preserve September ADRs and accepted members; this intake disposition does not reverse them.

facts: Explicit Resource Management reached TC39 Stage 4 and is expected in ECMAScript 2027.
Chromium ships the feature since 134, Firefox since 141, and Safari Technology Preview 250 provides preview support.
The report claim that Firefox does not regularly ship the feature is false.
XTend already owns explicit idempotent scheduler and surface-resource disposal lifecycles.
xtendHypotheses: A lab-only adapter can compare native lexical disposal with existing XTend cleanup invariants without changing public runtime contracts.
records.decisionRationale: No new raw evidence authorizes additional product adoption. Preserve September ADRs and accepted members; this intake disposition does not reverse them.

facts: W3C published ARIA in HTML as a Recommendation on 11 August 2026.
The Recommendation defines author-conformance rules and is not per-engine browser shipping evidence.
XTend has native-first runtime accessibility and hydration gates but no version-pinned ARIA-in-HTML rule matrix.
xtendHypotheses: A curated test-only conformance matrix can verify XTend SSR, pre-hydration and post-hydration markup without claiming complete AOM or assistive-technology interoperability.
records.decisionRationale: No new raw evidence authorizes additional product adoption. Preserve September ADRs and accepted members; this intake disposition does not reverse them.

facts: Scoped Custom Element Registries are a real Interop 2026 focus.
Chromium ships the feature and Firefox exposes experimental support behind a preference.
XTend components predominantly self-register in the global customElements registry.
xtendHypotheses: Registry injection in the RMT component adapter and Surface hosts may enable isolated tag namespaces.
Constructor exports and side-effect-free registration are prerequisites for broad scope support.
records.decisionRationale: No new raw evidence authorizes additional product adoption. Preserve September ADRs and accepted members; this intake disposition does not reverse them.

facts: scheduler.yield() provides prioritized continuations and is available in Chromium and Firefox 142.
The current XTend browser scheduler uses requestIdleCallback and timer fallbacks.
xtendHypotheses: An internal yieldContinuation capability may improve segmented hydration without changing RMT lane ownership.
records.decisionRationale: No new raw evidence authorizes additional product adoption. Preserve September ADRs and accepted members; this intake disposition does not reverse them.

facts: Navigation API is an Interop 2025 carry-over in Interop 2026, not a first-time 2026 focus.
The API reached Baseline Newly Available in 2026.
x-router owns navigation cancellation, focus, announcements and scroll restoration.
xtendHypotheses: A capability-gated host adapter may map native navigate events onto existing x-router lifecycle contracts.
records.decisionRationale: No new raw evidence authorizes additional product adoption. Preserve September ADRs and accepted members; this intake disposition does not reverse them.

facts: Interop 2026 targets dialog closedby, :open and popover=hint details rather than the already broadly available base APIs.
Native popovers are non-modal and cannot replace the modal x-popover contract without behavioral loss.
xtendHypotheses: Non-modal x-popover and x-tooltip can be evaluated separately from x-dialog and modal overlay ownership.
records.decisionRationale: No new raw evidence authorizes additional product adoption. Preserve September ADRs and accepted members; this intake disposition does not reverse them.
